newsitem.title: RWANDA: UN says Rwanda arrests five for UN monitor deaths.
newsitem.headline: UN says Rwanda arrests five for UN monitor deaths.

text.p: Rwandan security forces have arrested five of the suspected killers of four U.N. human rights monitors in western Rwanda, a U.N. human rights office spokesman said on Monday.
Jose Herrero, spokesman for the U.N. Human Rights Field Operation for Rwanda, said two others suspected of the killings were shot dead by Rwandan troops.
He said a team from the mission visited the five detainees in the southwestern town of Cyangugu on the weekend but the U.N. team was not permitted private interviews.
He said troops trying to arrest them last week shot dead the two other men, including one suspected by authorities of being the ringleader of the attack on the U.N. monitors.
"We cannot confirm all the evidence against them," said Herrero, adding local authorities said the five had confessed to the February 4 ambush.
Four monitors -- a Briton, a Cambodian and two Rwandans -- were killed and their Rwandan driver later died of his wounds.
Following the ambush, foreign aid agencies pulled international staff back to Kigali and moved non-essential staff to Nairobi, Kenya, for their security.
Three Spanish aid workers were killed in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri on January 18. A 61-year-old Canadian missionary was killed by a lone gunman north of Ruhengeri on February 2.
The government blamed Hutu militiamen who returned from Zaire and Tanzania with more than a million refugees in the last three months of last year for the attacks.
The Hutus fled Rwanda in 1994 during civil war, fearing reprisals for the three-month slaughter of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs.
The U.N. human rights office says Hutu death squads are killing Tutsi genocide survivors and witnesses to stop them denouncing the killers in the 1994 bloodbath.
